text: Since your urinalysis and ultrasound are normal, your flank pain and fever are likely not due to a kidney infection or obstruction. Did you experience any muscle aches or dark-colored urine during the week after taking your antibiotics? Also, have you noticed any swelling in your legs or face?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-associated acute interstitial nephritis (AIN).

Although your urinalysis and ultrasound are currently normal, your history of developing a rash after starting amoxicillin and cephalexin for sinusitis, followed by persistent fatigue and flank pain, is highly suggestive of drug-induced kidney inflammation. The symptoms resolved temporarily when the offending agent was changed, which is a classic presentation of AIN. Would you agree that the rash appeared shortly after initiating the first antibiotic?
